ayeaye: An aye-aye crouching low along a bare branch on all fours, seen from the side, with BOTH ITS FRONT HANDS PRESSED FLAT AND OPEN ON THE BARK beneath its shoulders, palms down, taking its weight. Every finger is spread out flat against the wood and touching it. On each hand the middle finger is NOTICEABLY LONGER AND MUCH THINNER than the four fingers beside it - a spidery bony finger lying flat along the bark among its neighbours, part of the same spread hand, one of five. Both hands are flat on the branch and the animal is not reaching, not pointing and not raising anything. Shaggy black-brown fur, huge round orange eyes, round thin dark ears, one long bushy tail hanging below the branch
baskingshark: A colossal harmless plankton-eating fish drifting with its jaws opened to their fullest, seen from a three-quarter front angle. The opening is a huge rounded funnel, and THE INSIDE OF THAT FUNNEL IS COMPLETELY EMPTY: a plain hollow cavern of deep shadow, dark and smooth and bare, with NOTHING VISIBLE ANYWHERE INSIDE IT - no pale shapes, no rows of anything, no vertical bars, no pattern, no texture, just unbroken darkness like the inside of an empty barrel or a cave at night. Around the edge of that opening, where the upper and lower jaw meet, runs A SMOOTH CONTINUOUS PALE GREY GUM LINE, a soft even band of bare rounded skin like the rolled rim of a rubber boot, plain and unbroken along its whole length with nothing growing from it. Five enormous gill slits wrap the head like stacked collars, a short blunt nose, small dark eyes far out at the sides, a bulky grey-brown body, a tall triangular fin, a crescent tail
sunfishmola: An ocean sunfish seen from the side, mouth at the front on the left. ITS BODY IS A TALL UPRIGHT OVAL STANDING ON ITS END - MUCH TALLER THAN IT IS LONG, about one and a half times as deep from the top of its back down to its belly as it is long from mouth to rear, so the silhouette is a high rounded slab like a shield stood upright, a millstone on its edge, a dinner plate balanced on its rim. It is emphatically NOT a long shape and NOT a horizontal shape - height is its largest dimension. The whole animal ENDS ABRUPTLY a short way behind the eye in a blunt vertical edge finished with a small wavy scalloped frill lying flat against it, and past that frill there is nothing at all. From the TOP one enormous pointed fin rises straight UP and from the BOTTOM an identical one points straight DOWN, each about as long as the body is deep. Rough mottled silver-grey hide, one round eye, a tiny round mouth, small pectoral fins
blackrhino_c: A newborn rhinoceros calf a few weeks old, seen HEAD-ON FROM DIRECTLY IN FRONT, facing the viewer square on, standing on four short legs. Everything about it is babyish: an oversized head, short stubby legs, a plump rounded body, enormous soft dark eyes set wide, and big soft rounded ears standing up on either side. Seen from this angle its face is a broad soft rounded shape, widest at the cheeks and narrowing gently to the muzzle, and THE WHOLE UPPER SURFACE OF ITS SNOUT IS BARE SMOOTH ROUNDED GREY SKIN, gently domed and completely blank, exactly like the smooth muzzle of a Labrador puppy or a young hippopotamus. ON TOP OF THAT SMOOTH SNOUT SITS ONE SMALL SOFT ROUNDED GREY KNOB, a low blunt bump about the size of its own eye, pebble-shaped and barely raised, sitting flat like a small river stone resting on a table - one low pebble and nothing else. Below it, a pointed hooked prehensile upper lip. Soft mid-grey hide, evenly lit
